SMTO-PRX-0012 — SMTO couldn't reach your Proxmox server

GUID: 563f49b5-69e0-476e-b420-d394ccc0a43a
Slug: proxmox-unreachable
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • SMTO tried to contact your Proxmox server through the Gateway but got no answer, or the Gateway wasn't ready to make the connection. If you asked for a change, it isn't certain whether it happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open System Health, or Settings › Setup › Gateways, and check that the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to reach other computers) is online. Every Proxmox request travels through the Gateway, so an offline Gateway means no reply.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select your Proxmox parameter, and check that "server" and "port" are correct; Proxmox normally uses port 8006. A wrong name, address or port sends the request somewhere nothing answers.
  3. On the computer running the Gateway, open the Proxmox web address in a browser to confirm the server is switched on and reachable from there. The Gateway's computer, not yours, is the one that has to reach Proxmox over the network.
  4. If you asked for a VM change, ask the Agent for that VM's current status before asking for the change again. A lost connection doesn't prove your change didn't happen.

What success looks like

  • The Agent returns your VM list or status from Proxmox.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your network. Don't assume a requested VM change didn't happen just because the connection failed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Proxmox request got no HTTP status after a Gateway transport failure, or the Gateway's HTTP readiness check failed before the Proxmox session was prepared.

What this means

  • The request has no HTTP status after a transport failure, or Gateway HTTP readiness fails before session preparation. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • The request has no HTTP status after a transport failure, or Gateway HTTP readiness fails before session preparation.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish Gateway readiness from target transport failure before attributing the issue to the Proxmox server itself.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the selected Gateway is connected and reports HTTP readiness, then test https://server:port/api2/json from the Gateway host (DNS, routing, firewall, port 8006) against the base URL in the Proxmox Server parameter. Read guest status before repeating any mutation; a transport failure is not proof that an earlier write did not run.
  • Verify the selected Gateway route, base URL and Proxmox service health.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended Gateway route and server endpoint provide a valid supported response.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
